items.title: Electrovacuum tensor Cauchy system

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity, Cambridge lecture notes, October 12 2022 revision, sections 6.2-6.4 and 10.4
references.locator: Section 6.2, equation (6.8), gives the covariant Maxwell equations in the (-+++) convention; section 6.3, equations (6.27)-(6.28), gives the Maxwell stress tensor and states its conservation as an exercise; section 6.4, equation (6.32), gives the Einstein equation; section 10.4, equations (10.24)-(10.26), gives the normal constraints. The notes use Gaussian normalization and c=1 in places; this definition instead records the SI normalization below.

references.title: M. Alcubierre, J. C. Degollado and M. Salgado, The Einstein-Maxwell system in 3+1 form and initial data for multiple charged black holes, arXiv:0907.1151v2
references.locator: Sections II.2-II.4, equations (70)-(89), state the electromagnetic stress tensor, its observer decomposition, the Einstein-Maxwell constraints, and the role of potential gauge. The paper uses Gaussian units and does not prove a coupled local existence theorem.

items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented and time-oriented four-manifold with smooth Lorentz metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Use its metric-selected connection and curvature convention. Fix $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and put

$$\kappa:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}>0.$$

Within this formulation, $c$, $G_N$, $\mu_0$, and $\Lambda$ are primitive model parameters: respectively, the time-to-length conversion parameter, the gravitational coupling parameter, the electromagnetic normalization parameter identified with vacuum permeability in the SI convention, and the coefficient of the cosmological term. Their values are not derived by this definition, and no numerical value or empirical exactness claim is made here. The coupling $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$ is derived from $G_N$ and $c$. For the SI interpretation, $c$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $G_N$ has units $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $\mu_0$ has units $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$, $\kappa$ has units $\mathrm{s^2\,kg^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$, and $\Lambda$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. In a length-coordinate chart $x^0=ct$, metric components are dimensionless and curvature components have units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$.

For a smooth real two-form $F\in\Omega^2(M)$, define

$$Q_{ab}(g,F):=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd},\qquad T^{\rm EM}_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}Q_{ab}(g,F).$$

Indices are raised with $g^{-1}$; $\star_g$ is the Lorentzian Hodge star of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. The electromagnetic stress tensor $T^{\rm EM}$ is a symmetric covariant two-tensor; in an orthonormal frame its components have energy-density units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. If $n$ is a future unit normal and $(\mathfrak e_1,\mathfrak e_2,\mathfrak e_3)$ is a positively oriented orthonormal spatial triad, define $e_i:=F(\mathfrak e_i,n)$ and $b_i:=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathfrak e_j,\mathfrak e_k)$. By [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]], these are $E_i/c$ and $B_i$ in the SI observer convention; both have units tesla.

For sign clarity only, a sourced extension would write $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0J^b$ for a smooth current vector $J$; the source-free system below is the case $J=0$.

The **source-free electrovacuum tensor Cauchy system** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is the system for a smooth Lorentz metric $g$ and smooth real two-form $F$ on $U$ given by

$$G_{ab}[g]+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T^{\rm EM}_{ab}[g,F],\qquad dF=0,\qquad d(\star_gF)=0.$$

Here $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Sg_{ab}$ is the Einstein tensor. A **spacelike initial hypersurface** is a smooth spacelike embedded three-manifold $i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow U$ with induced Riemannian metric $h=i^*g$ and future unit normal $n$, using [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]. Its second fundamental form is $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ for tangent vectors $X,Y$. The notation $K=\tfrac12\mathcal L_nh$ requires an induced-metric family: locally near each $p\in\Sigma$, define $\Phi(t,q)=\gamma_{q,n_q}(t)$ by the ambient geodesic with initial position $q$ and initial tangent $n_q$. Smooth dependence of geodesics and the inverse function theorem give, after shrinking around $(0,p)$, a local diffeomorphism $\Phi:(-\epsilon,\epsilon)\times V\to U_p$; its slices remain spacelike after a further shrinking. Put $h_t:=\Phi_t^*g$ on $V$. In local slice coordinates $y^i$, differentiating $(h_t)_{ij}=g_{ab}(\Phi(t,y))\partial_i\Phi^a\partial_j\Phi^b$ at $t=0$ gives
$$\left.\partial_t(h_t)_{ij}\right|_{0}=n^c\partial_cg_{ab}\,\partial_i\Phi^a\partial_j\Phi^b+g_{cb}(\partial_i n^c)\partial_j\Phi^b+g_{ac}\partial_i\Phi^a(\partial_jn^c)=g(\nabla_{\partial_i}n,\partial_j\Phi)+g(\nabla_{\partial_j}n,\partial_i\Phi)=2K_{ij},$$
using metric compatibility, torsion-freeness and symmetry of $K$. Thus $\mathcal L_nh$ denotes only this initial derivative of the local induced-metric family; no global normal foliation or uniform time width is assumed. A hypersurface is a **Cauchy hypersurface in $U$** exactly when every inextendible causal curve $\gamma:I\to U$ meets it at exactly one parameter value, that is, $\gamma^{-1}[i(\Sigma)]$ has exactly one element, using the causal-curve convention of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]. The local initial-data constructions require a spacelike initial hypersurface; they do not assume this global intersection property. The initial data are the induced $(h,K,e,b)$, where $e,b$ are the spatial fields just defined. No global electromagnetic potential is part of this definition.

In the SI convention the electromagnetic two-form has orthonormal-frame components in tesla, $T^{\rm EM}_{ab}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and every term of the Einstein equation has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. The equations define a mathematical model; they do not assert that the model describes nature or that arbitrary Cauchy data have a development.

items.title: Causal solutions, Killing horizons, escape and metric extensions

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity, Cambridge lecture notes, October 12 2022 revision
references.locator: Causal structure and stationary black-hole terminology; the selected-model escape observable, signed normalization and well-definedness are specified locally below.

items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth Hausdorff second-countable boundaryless four-manifold with smooth Lorentz metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and smooth time orientation. All definitions below are mathematical. A solution of a specified covariant field system is a tuple of fields of the regularity stated by that system satisfying its equations on its stated domain; this terminology alone supplies neither existence nor a global electromagnetic potential.

**(a) Global causal and Cauchy conventions.** Use exactly [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]: a future causal curve is locally absolutely continuous in coordinate charts, has nonzero future causal derivative almost everywhere, and has no constant subinterval. Inextendibility and causal reachability $J^\pm$ have that item's endpoint-extension meanings. A Cauchy set meets every inextendible causal curve at exactly one parameter value: its inverse image under each such curve is a singleton, as in [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]. A spacelike hypersurface is a smooth embedded codimension-one submanifold with positive-definite induced metric; this local condition does not assert the global Cauchy property. Strong causality has the small-neighborhood no-leaving-and-reentering meaning of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]]. Global hyperbolicity means strong causality and compactness of every $J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$, exactly as there; no equivalence theorem is added here.

**(b) Null and Killing horizons.** A smooth embedded hypersurface $H\subset M$ is **null** when $g|_{TH}$ is degenerate. Equivalently, for any local defining function $f$ with $H=\{f=0\}$ and $df\ne0$ on $H$, $g^{-1}(df,df)=0$ on $H$. A specified smooth vector field $\xi$ is **Killing** when $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$, equivalently $\nabla_{(a}\xi_{b)}=0$, using [[def-gr-killing-field]] and [[thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities]]. A **Killing horizon for $\xi$** is a null hypersurface whose nonzero-generator part $H_*:=\{p\in H:\xi_p\ne0\}$ is nonempty and dense in $H$, and on that part the specified field is tangent, null and normal: $\xi_p\in T_pH$ and $g(\xi_p,X)=0$ for every $X\in T_pH$. A generator parameter or asymptotic normalization, when required, must be specified separately.

On $H_*$ the **signed surface gravity** for this precise $\xi$ is the unique smooth scalar $\kappa_H$ such that

$$d\bigl(g(\xi,\xi)\bigr)_p=-2\kappa_H(p)\,\xi^\flat_p\quad(p\in H_*).$$

This is an equality of ambient covectors at points of $H$, not merely of their pullbacks to $TH$. No constancy or positivity is asserted. Under a nonzero constant rescaling $\xi'=a\xi$, $\kappa'_H=a\kappa_H$. A **bifurcation surface** is a specified smooth spacelike two-surface $B$ where the extended Killing field vanishes and the specified horizon branches meet (or have $B$ as their common boundary). Surface gravity at such a surface means a smooth extension of the scalar from the adjacent nonzero-generator portions, with each point in their closure, only if that extension exists; the defining equation at $\xi=0$ alone determines no value. Neither a bifurcation surface nor such an extension is asserted to exist.

**(c) Sections, area and ergoregions.** A **horizon section** is a specified smooth spacelike embedded two-surface $S$ in the horizon, with positive induced metric $h$. Its area density is $\mu_h=\sqrt{\det(h_{ij})}\,|dy^1dy^2|$ of [[def-riemannian-volume-density]]. Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) for intrinsic density integration, as in [[def-riemannian-volume-of-a-compactly-supported-smooth-density]]. Its possibly infinite area is the nonnegative extended value

$$\operatorname{Area}_g(S):=\sup\left\{\int_S\chi\mu_h:\chi\in C_c^\infty(S),\ 0\le\chi\le1\right\}\in[0,+\infty],$$

with the extended order of [[def-extended-reals]]. On compact $S$ this is $\int_S\mu_h$; orientation is unnecessary. The density glues by [[lem-the-riemannian-volume-density-is-coordinate-independent]]. A stationary field here is a specified Killing field timelike on a specified nonempty open region; no normalization is inferred from this adjective. Its **ergoregion** in the chosen model is $\{g(\xi,\xi)>0\}$, its **stationary-limit set** is $\{g(\xi,\xi)=0\}$, and its **ergosurface** is the relative boundary of its ergoregion. Every ergosurface point lies in the stationary-limit set; the converse requires a separate sign-change argument. Nullness, Killing-horizon status and escape-boundary status are separate claims; a coordinate root alone proves none of them.

**(d) Selected-model escape.** Fix a specified open spacetime model $U\subseteq M$ and specified smooth radius observable $r:U\to\mathbb R$. An admissible escape path is a continuous $\gamma:[0,T)\to U$, $0<T\le+\infty$, with $\gamma(0)=p$, such that every compact parameter segment has a finite subdivision on whose pieces the coordinate curve is $C^1$, with nonzero future causal tangent (one-sided at piece endpoints). Define

$$\mathcal E_{U,r}:=\left\{p\in U:\exists\gamma\text{ admissible from }p\ \forall R>0\ \exists t\in[0,T):r(\gamma(t))>R\right\}.$$

The **selected escape boundary** is $\partial_U\mathcal E_{U,r}$. This explicitly selected piecewise-$C^1$ path class is contained in the global causal-curve class of (a); it does not replace that class in Cauchy definitions. No geodesic restriction, conformal completion, event-horizon identification or maximal extension is implicit in this definition.

**(e) Approached metric extensions and curvature obstructions.** A $C^2$ nondegenerate metric extension of an open model $(U,g)$ consists of a smooth Hausdorff second-countable four-manifold $\widetilde M$, a $C^2$ Lorentz metric $\widetilde g$ of the same signature, and a smooth open embedding $j:U\to\widetilde M$ with $j^*\widetilde g=g$. An **approached added point** is $p\in\widetilde M\setminus j(U)$ with $j(x_n)\to p$ for a specified sequence $x_n\in U$ (or the corresponding limit of a specified curve). An **extension obstruction at that approach** means no such extension and added point can realize the stated approach. In particular, unbounded absolute values of a polynomial complete contraction of the curvature tensor and metric inverse along $x_n$ obstruct such an approached $C^2$ nondegenerate extension. This criterion concerns curvature without its covariant derivatives. A smooth metric extension is the same definition with smooth $\widetilde g$. These notions alone assert neither a distributional matter source nor geodesic incompleteness.

**(f) Observers and spatial fields.** Observers, smooth observer congruences and their integral curves, adapted charts and tetrads retain the distinct meanings of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Relative to a future unit observer $n$, an electric or magnetic spatial covector is identified with a spatial vector only by raising with the positive rest metric $h=g+n^\flat\otimes n^\flat$ on $n^\perp$. Such spatial vectors $e,b$ are not tetrad basis vectors. No singular-source product or action is defined by this vocabulary.

items.title: Periodic high-Sobolev state spaces

references.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Lecture Notes in Physics 540 (2000), section 3.1
references.locator: Section 3.1, pages 28-31, defines the periodic Sobolev setting used for symmetric-hyperbolic evolution and its regularity thresholds. The exact local Sobolev interface used here is the current published GR14 definition, not the source's inaccurate composition estimate.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity, Cambridge lecture notes, October 12 2022 revision, sections 10.4-10.5
references.locator: Section 10.4 fixes the induced metric and second fundamental form data convention; section 10.5 states the initial-value setting.

items.statement:
For the geometric data convention, orient $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ by the ordered dimensionless coordinates $(\theta^1,\theta^2,\theta^3)$; the corresponding length-coordinate frame $(\partial_{X^1},\partial_{X^2},\partial_{X^3})$ has the same orientation.

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as required by [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]] and [[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]]; no use of the full Axiom of Choice is made here. Let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, its normalized measure, the componentwise real Sobolev spaces $H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, and their weak-derivative and Fourier-coefficient conventions be exactly those of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. In particular, $H^s$ is defined for integer $s\ge0$, the weak-derivative norm is equivalent to the Fourier-weight norm by [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]], and the trigonometric characters are a complete orthonormal system by [[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]]. A field is a function with the domain and codomain declaration of [[def-function]]; Sobolev fields are its $L^2$-equivalence classes, not pointwise representatives.

For finite $m\ge1$, open $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, compact $K\subseteq O$, $R\ge0$, and integer $s\ge5$, define the bounded admissible initial-state class

$$\mathcal S_s(K,R):=\{u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m):u_0\text{ has its continuous representative valued in }K,\ \|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R\}.$$

The representative is unique because two continuous functions equal almost everywhere on the torus agree everywhere. For a smooth periodic first-order reduction of the electrovacuum equations, its specified finite list of real state components is identified with one such $\mathbb R^m$-valued function; the state-component convention is part of that reduction. In the geometric data convention below, the component arrays are specified separately. This is a definition of admissible function-space classes only; it asserts no existence result for a coupled Einstein-Maxwell reduction.

For the geometric data convention, write the dimensionless torus coordinate as $\theta^i\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ and introduce a fixed length scale $L_0>0$ in metres. The corresponding length coordinates are $X^i=L_0\theta^i$ on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi L_0}:=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi L_0\mathbb Z)^3$; the Sobolev variable remains $\theta$, and $X$ is not a second name for a coordinate on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$. The arrays $h_{ij}(\theta)$ and $K_{ij}(\theta)$ are the covariant metric and second-fundamental-form components in the length-coordinate frame $\partial_{X^i}$, with $h_{ij}=h_{ji}$ and $K_{ij}=K_{ji}$. Let $\mathsf e_A(h)$, $A=1,2,3$, be the positively oriented $h$-orthonormal frame obtained by Gram-Schmidt from the ordered global frame $(\partial_{X^1},\partial_{X^2},\partial_{X^3})$. For spatial vectors $e,b$, the electromagnetic component arrays in this convention are $e_A:=h(e,\mathsf e_A)$ and $b_A:=h(b,\mathsf e_A)$; these are the orthonormal observer components used in the Einstein-Maxwell first-order reduction. The frame coefficients are smooth functions of the positive matrix $(h_{ij})$. If $h\in H^{s+1}$ has range in a compact subset of the positive-definite matrices, the composition supplier gives these coefficients in $H^{s+1}$; since $s\ge5$, the Sobolev-algebra supplier gives their products with coordinate vector components in $H^s$. The inverse frame matrix has the same property, so the coordinate and orthonormal component arrays describe the same $H^s$ vector fields.

Thus the data component spaces mean $(h_{ij})\in H^{s+1}(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^9)$ with values in symmetric positive matrices, $(K_{ij})\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^9)$ with values in symmetric matrices, and $(e_A),(b_A)\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^3)$. A smooth periodic first-order state also includes the specified component functions of that reduction and the first spatial metric derivatives; in the above length-coordinate convention $v_{kij}:=\partial_{X^k}h_{ij}=L_0^{-1}\partial_{\theta^k}h_{ij}$ and $K_{ij}$ carry one inverse-length factor. For a fixed field scale $F_0>0$ in tesla, the dimensionless physical component arrays are $h_{ij}$, $L_0K_{ij}$, $L_0v_{kij}$, $e_A/F_0$, and $b_A/F_0$. Each fixed rescaling is invertible and preserves the finite-component Sobolev topology. These are component and unit conventions, not additional field equations.

items.title: Exact periodic positive symmetric-hyperbolic supplier

references.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Lecture Notes in Physics 540 (2000), section 3.1
references.locator: Section 3.1 states the quasilinear symmetric-hyperbolic system class and discusses its local existence, uniqueness, stability and smooth persistence. Its proof sketch is not used in place of the exact current GR14 suppliers cited below.

items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $A^\mu,B$ ($\mu=0,1,2,3$) be a periodic symmetric-hyperbolic coefficient family on $I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$ in the exact sense of [[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]: the coefficient maps are smooth, each $A^\mu$ is a real symmetric matrix, and $A^0$ is positive definite. Let $K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact and let $R\ge0$. Then there are $T>0$ and $C<\infty$, uniform over all $u_0\in\mathcal S_s(K,R)$ of [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]], such that the system

$$A^0(t,x,u)\partial_tu+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,x,u)\partial_i u+B(t,x,u)=0$$

has a unique Sobolev solution $u:(-T,T)\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ with $u(0)=u_0$, values in $K'$, $u\in L^\infty H^s\cap C^0H^{s-1}$, and $\partial_tu\in L^\infty H^{s-1}$. The corresponding norm and time-derivative bounds are those in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]]. Solutions are unique in the stated bounded classical class and depend continuously on initial data in $H^{s-1}$ by [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-uniqueness-stability]]. If $u_0$ is smooth, the same solution is smooth on this same interval by [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-smooth-persistence]].

This theorem supplies only the analytic conclusion for a system whose coefficient hypotheses have already been verified. It does not assert that a particular gauge-fixed Einstein-Maxwell reduction has these matrices; that is a separate mathematical obligation.

items.title: Maxwell stress algebra and covariant conservation

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity, Cambridge lecture notes, October 12 2022 revision, sections 6.2-6.3
references.locator: Section 6.2, equation (6.8), states the curved-spacetime Maxwell equations in Reall's Gaussian convention; section 6.3, equations (6.27)-(6.28), gives the Maxwell stress tensor and identifies stress conservation as a consequence to prove.

references.title: M. Alcubierre, J. C. Degollado and M. Salgado, The Einstein-Maxwell system in 3+1 form and initial data for multiple charged black holes, arXiv:0907.1151v2
references.locator: Section II.2, equations (70)-(78), computes the Maxwell stress tensor, trace, energy density and Poynting component in a 3+1 split; its Gaussian factor 1/(4 pi) is replaced here by the declared SI factor mu_0^{-1}.

items.statement:
Let $F$ be a smooth real two-form on a smooth oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with the connection, Hodge star, and tensor $Q_{ab}=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\tfrac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}$ of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]]. For a smooth vector field $J$, suppose

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0J^b.$$

Then $Q_{ab}$ is symmetric and trace-free, and the SI-normalized stress tensor $T^{\rm EM}_{ab}=\mu_0^{-1}Q_{ab}$ satisfies

$$\nabla^aT^{\rm EM}_{ab}=-F_{bc}J^c.$$

In the source-free case $J=0$, $\nabla^aT^{\rm EM}_{ab}=0$. If $n$ is a future unit normal and $(\mathfrak e_1,\mathfrak e_2,\mathfrak e_3)$ a positively oriented orthonormal spatial triad, put $e_i:=F(\mathfrak e_i,n)$, $b_i:=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathfrak e_j,\mathfrak e_k)$, and $(e\times b)_i:=\epsilon_{ijk}e_jb_k$. Then

$$T^{\rm EM}(n,n)=\frac{|e|^2+|b|^2}{2\mu_0},\qquad T^{\rm EM}(n,\mathfrak e_i)=-\frac{(e\times b)_i}{\mu_0}.$$

These are pointwise tensor identities. In the SI interpretation $e=E/c$ and $b=B$ have units tesla; no measurement or physical applicability claim is included.

items.title: Lorenz potential wave contains Ricci coupling

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity, Cambridge lecture notes, October 12 2022 revision, sections 4.2 and 6.2
references.locator: Section 4.2 fixes the vector Ricci identity and curvature sign; section 6.2, equation (6.8), states the Maxwell equations in a curved spacetime.

references.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Lecture Notes in Physics 540 (2000), section 3.2
references.locator: Section 3.2, page 84, states that source-free Maxwell fields are locally represented by potentials and flags the gauge and nontrivial-topology distinction; the Ricci identity is derived completely below from the current GR supplier.

items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the Lorentzian geometry and use the curvature convention of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $A_a$ be a smooth one-form, $A^a:=g^{ab}A_b$, and $F:=dA$, so $F_{ab}=\nabla_aA_b-\nabla_bA_a$ by torsion-freeness. Define $\Box_gA_b:=\nabla^a\nabla_aA_b$ and $\operatorname{div}A:=\nabla_aA^a$. Then

$$\nabla^aF_{ab}=\Box_gA_b-\nabla_b(\operatorname{div}A)-\operatorname{Ric}_{bc}A^c.$$

Consequently, if $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0J^b$, the Lorenz condition $\operatorname{div}A=0$ makes the potential equation

$$\Box_gA_b-\operatorname{Ric}_{bc}A^c=-\mu_0J_b.$$

The curvature term is part of the identity; this is not an uncoupled collection of scalar metric wave equations. The statement is local in the sense that it assumes a potential $A$ is already defined on the open set under consideration; it does not assert a global potential for every closed $F$.

items.title: Local potential homotopy and Lorenz gauge reachability

references.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Lecture Notes in Physics 540 (2000), sections 3.2 and 3.3
references.locator: Section 3.2, page 84, records local potential representation for a closed Maxwell field and warns that nontrivial spatial topology can obstruct a global potential; sections 3.1-3.2 discuss local symmetric-hyperbolic Cauchy theory.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity, Cambridge lecture notes, October 12 2022 revision, sections 8.1 and 8.7
references.locator: Sections 8.1 and 8.7 define differential forms and Stokes' theorem; the local homotopy and gauge wave are proved below.

items.statement:
Let $U$ be a coordinate neighborhood whose image in $\mathbb R^4$ is star-shaped about the origin, and let $F$ be a smooth real two-form on $U$ with $dF=0$. In those coordinates define

$$A_a(x):=\int_0^1 t x^b F_{ba}(tx)\,dt.$$

Then $A$ is a smooth one-form on $U$ and $dA=F$ there. This is a local potential statement only.

For the gauge assertion, let $g$ be a smooth Lorentz metric on a neighborhood of a smooth spacelike hypersurface patch $S$, and let $A$ be a smooth one-form already defined on that neighborhood. Near each point of $S$ there is a smaller neighborhood and a smooth scalar $\chi$ such that

$$A':=A+d\chi,\qquad dA'=dA,\qquad \nabla^aA'_a=0.$$

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the symmetric-hyperbolic supplier [[thm-gr-local-symmetric-hyperbolic-well-posedness]]. The gauge proof constructs local Gaussian-normal coordinates with $x^0=0$ on the slice, $g_{00}=-1$, $g_{0i}=0$, and $(g^{ij})$ positive definite. No global potential or global gauge choice is asserted. When the Lorenz condition is combined with the Maxwell equation for a potential, [[prop-emg-potential-ricci-wave-identity]] retains the Ricci term.

items.title: Constrained electrovacuum initial data

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity, Cambridge lecture notes, October 12 2022 revision, sections 10.3-10.5
references.locator: Section 10.4, equations (10.24)-(10.26), defines the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints using h and K=1/2 L_n h; section 10.5 describes the Cauchy data.

references.title: M. Alcubierre, J. C. Degollado and M. Salgado, The Einstein-Maxwell system in 3+1 form and initial data for multiple charged black holes, arXiv:0907.1151v2
references.locator: Section II.3, equations (79)-(80), writes the electromagnetic Hamiltonian and momentum sources; its conventions are translated to the SI-normalized stress tensor and the stated positive K convention.

items.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty, smooth, oriented three-manifold without boundary. Let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and let $e,b$ be smooth vector fields tangent to $\Sigma$. For data induced on an embedded spacelike slice $i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$, let $n$ be its future unit normal, let $F$ be the smooth two-form of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], and define spatial covectors $\mathcal E,\mathcal B\in\Omega^1(\Sigma)$ by $\mathcal E(X):=F(X,n)$ and $\mathcal B(X):=-({\star_gF})(X,n)$ for $X\in T\Sigma$. Identify these with vector fields using the positive metric $h$: $e:=\sharp_h\mathcal E$ and $b:=\sharp_h\mathcal B$, so in any coordinates $e^i=h^{ij}\mathcal E_j$ and $b^i=h^{ij}\mathcal B_j$. Equivalently, $\mathcal E$ is the restriction of the observer electric covector $E/c$ and $\mathcal B$ the restriction of the observer magnetic covector $B$ of [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. For an abstract data tuple not assumed to come from $F$, $e,b$ are simply the specified tangent vector fields. This fixes the convention without adding a potential or an existence assumption.

For the observer-covector comparison above, the smooth normal along $\Sigma$ has local smooth ambient extensions by [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]; shrinking and normalizing an extension gives an observer congruence to which [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]] applies. The restrictions $\mathcal E,\mathcal B$ depend only on $n|_\Sigma$, so they are independent of the chosen extension.

Write $h^{ij}$ for the inverse matrix to $h_{ij}$ and use $h$ to raise every spatial index. Let $D$ and $R(h)$ denote the Levi-Civita connection and scalar curvature of $h$, set $\tau:=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2:=h^{ik}h^{j\ell}K_{ij}K_{k\ell}$, and choose the induced spatial orientation so $\operatorname{vol}_g=\theta^0\wedge\operatorname{vol}_h=-n^\flat\wedge\operatorname{vol}_h$ in a positively oriented normal coframe with $\theta^0(n)=1$. Define the spatial cross product by $h(e\times_hb,w)=\operatorname{vol}_h(e,b,w)$ for each tangent vector $w$.

For the fixed parameters $(\kappa,\Lambda,\mu_0)$ of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], the tuple $(\Sigma,h,K,e,b)$ is **constrained electrovacuum initial data** when

$$D_ie^i=0,\qquad D_ib^i=0,$$

$$R(h)+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}\bigl(|e|_h^2+|b|_h^2\bigr),$$

$$D^jK_{ji}-D_i\tau=-\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}(e\times_hb)_i.$$

Here the last display is an equality of covectors. The scalar-curvature form is the Gauss-Codazzi form of the normal projections in [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]; the sign and $K$ convention are those of [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] and [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]]. This definition asserts no existence or uniqueness of a spacetime development.

For the periodic high-regularity class, use the dimensionless coordinate $\theta^i$ and length coordinate $X^i=L_0\theta^i$ of [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]], for a fixed $L_0>0$. The arrays $h_{ij}$ and $K_{ij}$ are the length-coordinate covariant components with $h_{ij}\in H^{s+1}$ and $K_{ij}\in H^s$. The Sobolev components of $e,b$ are $e_A=h(e,\mathsf e_A)$ and $b_A=h(b,\mathsf e_A)$ in the canonical positively oriented $h$-orthonormal frame $\mathsf e_A$ specified there; thus $e_A,b_A\in H^s$. If $\mathsf e_A=E_A^i\partial_{X^i}$, their coordinate components are $e^i=E_A^i e_A$ and $b^i=E_A^i b_A$. The coefficients $E_A^i$ are smooth functions of the positive matrix $h_{ij}$; on the compact range of each such metric, [[lem-gr-smooth-composition-and-commutator-estimates]] puts them in $H^{s+1}$ and [[lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-algebra]] makes the coordinate components $H^s$ as well.

For these representatives define the spatial connection coefficients by $\Gamma(h)^k{}_{ij}=\tfrac12h^{k\ell}(\partial_{X^i}h_{j\ell}+\partial_{X^j}h_{i\ell}-\partial_{X^\ell}h_{ij})$, with $\partial_{X^i}=L_0^{-1}\partial_{\theta^i}$. On coordinate vector components put $D_i e^j=\partial_{X^i}e^j+\Gamma(h)^j{}_{ik}e^k$ and $D_i b^j=\partial_{X^i}b^j+\Gamma(h)^j{}_{ik}b^k$; on the covariant tensor $K$ put $D_iK_{jk}=\partial_{X^i}K_{jk}-\Gamma(h)^\ell{}_{ij}K_{\ell k}-\Gamma(h)^\ell{}_{ik}K_{j\ell}$. Define $R(h)$ by $R^a{}_{bij}=\partial_{X^i}\Gamma(h)^a{}_{jb}-\partial_{X^j}\Gamma(h)^a{}_{ib}+\Gamma(h)^a{}_{ic}\Gamma(h)^c{}_{jb}-\Gamma(h)^a{}_{jc}\Gamma(h)^c{}_{ib}$, followed by the Ricci and scalar contractions of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Sobolev embedding gives $h\in C^{s-1}$ and $K,e,b\in C^{s-2}$; the uniform positive lower eigenvalue makes $h^{-1}$ well defined, and the smooth-composition and algebra suppliers give $\Gamma(h)\in H^s$, $R(h)\in H^{s-1}$, and $D K,D e,D b\in H^{s-1}$. Since $s\ge5$, these constraint terms have continuous representatives, and their displayed equalities mean pointwise equality of those representatives. In the SI interpretation, $K$ and $D$ carry one inverse-length factor, $R(h)$ and $\Lambda$ carry inverse-length squared, and the orthonormal components $e_A,b_A$ have units tesla; the factors $\kappa/\mu_0$ give matching units in the constraints. No numerical parameter values are assigned here.

items.title: Gauss-Codazzi and Maxwell initial constraints

references.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Lecture Notes in Physics 540 (2000), sections 2.2 and 2.4
references.locator: Section 2.2, equations (2.10)-(2.13), derives the normal constraint equations from Gauss-Codazzi; section 2.4 discusses the initial-value split. The complete local proof used here is thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame.

references.title: M. Alcubierre, J. C. Degollado and M. Salgado, The Einstein-Maxwell system in 3+1 form and initial data for multiple charged black holes, arXiv:0907.1151v2
references.locator: Sections II.2-II.3, equations (75)-(80), gives the Maxwell energy/momentum sources and Hamiltonian/momentum constraints in Gaussian units; the proof here converts to the declared SI normalization.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity, Cambridge lecture notes, October 12 2022 revision, sections 10.3-10.4
references.locator: Section 10.3 states the Gauss-Codazzi equations and marks their proofs non-examinable; section 10.4 derives the normal-normal and normal-tangential constraint projections.

items.statement:
Let $(g,F)$ be a smooth source-free electrovacuum solution of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]] on a neighborhood of a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface $i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$. Let $n$ be its future unit normal, $h=i^*g$, $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$, and let $(e,b)$ be its observer electric/magnetic data. Then the induced tuple $(\Sigma,h,K,e,b)$ satisfies all four constraints in [[def-emg-constrained-electrovacuum-data]], namely the two Maxwell divergence constraints and

$$R(h)+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}(|e|_h^2+|b|_h^2),$$

$$D^jK_{ji}-D_i\operatorname{tr}_hK=-\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}(e\times_hb)_i.$$

This is a necessary-constraint theorem for an existing smooth solution. It is not a sufficiency or local-existence theorem for arbitrary data satisfying these equations.

items.title: Harmonic initial data relative to a fixed smooth background

references.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Lecture Notes in Physics 540 (2000), section 2.4 and section 5.1
references.locator: Section 2.4 describes the harmonic-map reduction; section 5.1 constructs reduced initial data from (h,K). The finite-regularity fixed-background correction is proved here.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity, Cambridge lecture notes, October 12 2022 revision, sections 10.2-10.5
references.locator: Sections 10.2-10.4 define the extrinsic-curvature convention and constraint data; the local harmonic data computation is supplied by this item's proof.

items.statement:
Let $s\ge5$ be an integer and $L_0>0$. Let the underlying periodic manifold be $\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi L_0}$ with length coordinates $X^i$, and use the diffeomorphism $D_{L_0}:\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\Sigma$, $[\theta]\mapsto[L_0\theta]$, to parametrize its component functions as in [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]]. This map is well defined with smooth inverse $[X]\mapsto[X/L_0]$. Let $(h,K,e,b)$ be periodic data of [[def-emg-constrained-electrovacuum-data]] with $h\in H^{s+1}$, $K,e,b\in H^s$ and a uniform positive lower eigenvalue bound for the continuous representative of $h$. Here Sobolev membership means membership of the length-frame component arrays $h_{ij},K_{ij}$ and the specified orthonormal arrays $e_A,b_A$, composed with $D_{L_0}$, in the spaces on the dimensionless torus; it does not mean the components of the pulled-back tensors. All spatial derivatives below are $\partial_{X^i}=L_0^{-1}\partial_{\theta^i}$. Fix a smooth positive reference metric $\gamma$ on $\Sigma$ and use the product background $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\gamma_{ij}(X)dX^i dX^j$ near $\{x^0=0\}\times\Sigma$. Define

$$Q^i:=h^{jk}\bigl(\Gamma(h)^i{}_{jk}-\Gamma(\gamma)^i{}_{jk}\bigr),$$

where the difference of the two spatial Levi-Civita connections is a tensor. Prescribe the spacetime metric Cauchy $1$-jet at $x^0=0$ by

$$g_{ij}=h_{ij},\quad g_{00}=-1,\quad g_{0i}=0,\quad \partial_0g_{ij}=2K_{ij},\quad \partial_0g_{00}=-2\operatorname{tr}_hK,\quad \partial_0g_{0i}=h_{ij}Q^j.$$

For this jet, let $g_0^{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,h^{ij})$ be the inverse metric block on the slice and define its Christoffel value by

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}[j^1_0g]:=\tfrac12 g_0^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{db}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr)\big|_{x^0=0}.$$

Define the initial-slice harmonic-gauge vector directly from the prescribed $1$-jet by

$$H_0^a:=g_0^{bc}\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}[j^1_0g]-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\bigr)\big|_{x^0=0}.$$

This is the initial value of the harmonic-gauge vector of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]] for every $C^1$ metric on a neighborhood realizing the prescribed jet; no neighborhood extension is needed to define $H_0$. Each metric value in the jet is $H^{s+1}$ and each prescribed first derivative is $H^s$, so the displayed algebraic expression has an $H^s$ representative. It vanishes on the initial slice. The background $\gamma$ is required to be smooth; choosing $\gamma=h$ is not asserted to be valid for finite-regularity $h$.

items.title: Flat zero-field data and Minkowski development
items.statement: Take $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, Minkowski metric $g=-(dx^0)^2+(dx^1)^2+(dx^2)^2+(dx^3)^2$, the standard orientation and future direction, and the hypersurface $\Sigma=\{x^0=0\}$. Set $F=0$ and $\Lambda=0$, with the fixed positive parameters $\kappa,\mu_0$ of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]]. The induced data are $h=\delta$, $K=0$, and $e=b=0$. This is a smooth exact solution and its data satisfy all four electrovacuum constraints.

items.title: Nonzero flat test field is not a coupled flat solution
items.statement: For $\Lambda=0$, every smooth source-free Maxwell field on a prescribed Minkowski metric is an electrovacuum solution with that same flat metric.

items.title: Magnetic period obstructs a global potential
items.statement: Let $M=\mathbb R^{1,1}\times\mathbb T^2_L$ with flat product metric, where $\mathbb T^2_L=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^2$ has length coordinates $x^1,x^2$ of period $L>0$. For $B_0\ne0$, define the smooth two-form $F=B_0\,dx^1\wedge dx^2$, with $B_0$ in tesla in the SI interpretation. Then $F$ is closed and source-free on the flat background, and its period over the spatial two-torus is $B_0L^2\ne0$. The field has local potentials but no single-valued global one-form potential on $M$. This example concerns the Maxwell field-strength sector on a fixed flat background; it is not asserted to solve the coupled Einstein equation with that flat metric.
